newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee weakens vs fwd dlr on RBI purchases.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee weakens vs fwd dlr on RBI purchases.

text.p: The Indian rupee weakened against the forward dollar in afternoon trade Thursday with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) buying dollars, dealers said.
They said forward premiums rose on RBI forward dollar purchases. They said the central bank bought outright dollars for May, June and July delivery.
May delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 3/5 paise against opening quotes of 2/4, June dollars at 12/15 against 10/12 and July at 25/30 against 24/26.
November delivery dollars were quoted 87/92 paise against opening quotes of 86/88, dealers said.
The spot rupee was quoted 35.82/83 per dollar in afternoon trade after being stuck in a narrow range between 35.815 and 35.825 for most of the day, dealers said.
In latest deals the rupee was quoted 35.815/822 per dollar.
Dealers said the RBI bought dollars both in spot and forward markets.
"They (RBI) bought spot-dollars at 35.815 and up to 35.825," said a dealer. "But the amounts do not seem to be big."
